correctness.rationale: Reconstructed exact domain 3-by-3 Hermitian PSD trace-one, t in [1/3,1], m integer >=3. Orthogonal diagonal/offdiagonal trace-square split yields u<=t-1/3. The cubic trace equals six times real triangular product and AM-GM gives v^2<=u^3/6. Cayley-Hamilton recurrence with nonnegative coefficients and strict positive v^2 term at every even order >=6 gives the sharp moment bound. Equality requires flat diagonal/edge moduli and holonomy 0 or pi. Explicit eigenvalues prove the negative branch is PSD iff t<=1/2; all positive forms have exact purity. Determinant and principal-minor criteria give the complete entrywise-l1 phase family. The extracted standalone verifier passed 41205 checks; finite checks cannot establish the universal theorem.

originality.rationale: The 2015 purity–entrywise-l1 bound and its positive-sign maximizers are explicitly credited. Direct comparison of Theorem 2, its Eq. (9), and the proof shows that a negative phase triangle has identical entrywise-l1 optimum, is PSD through purity 1/2, and has a gauge-invariant sign not represented by the positive pseudo-pure family. New claims are the sharp all-higher-even Schatten norms, their complete equality classes, and the 1/2 phase cutoff. The Schatten-p coherence functionals of Rana et al. and later Streltsov et al. minimize over diagonal states, unlike the fixed dephasing norm here. Yao et al. study quadratic/Frobenius information rather than sixth and higher moments. The closest published research-index hits study different objects. A historical unindexed equivalent remains possible.

value.rationale: The sharp family of higher-even spectral coherence magnitudes is a natural purity-conditioned matrix invariant, not a made-up slice. It exposes a gauge-invariant phase distinction invisible to Frobenius and entrywise-l1 extrema, gives all equality matrices for arbitrarily many natural even powers, and establishes a sharp positivity cutoff t=1/2. It clarifies a materially overrestricted earlier pseudo-pure maximizing-family assertion without claiming the existing l1 numerical optimum as new. The result is quantitatively useful for spectral sensitivity of qutrit offdiagonal matrices, without pretending to be a coherence monotone or a general quantum resource theorem.
